$description: ViaVitae colour tokens — the single source of truth for every colour in every ViaVitae product, site and document. Format: W3C Design Tokens Community Group draft (groups are plain objects; leaf nodes carry $type and $value). Consumed by build/css/tokens.css, build/tailwind.preset.ts, build/ts/index.ts and build/figma-tokens/tokens.json. Edit this file and rebuild; never hand-edit a build output.

meta.$description: Non-DTCG bookkeeping, ignored by DTCG-conformant tooling.
meta.name: colors

color.$description: All colour tokens, in three tiers: palette (raw ramps, never referenced by a component), semantic (theme-aware roles a component consumes) and chart (data-visualisation series). A component references the semantic tier only. Referencing the palette tier directly is a review blocker, because a palette value does not change when the theme changes and the component silently breaks on a dark surface.

palette.$description: Raw colour ramps. Each ramp is a monotone lightness ladder in HSL space anchored on the brand value, so a step number means the same relative lightness in every family. Anchors are fixed by ADR-001 and may not drift.

navy.$description: Brand navy. Anchor #0E1B3D at step 900. The structural colour: headers, footers, dark surfaces, primary text on light backgrounds.

50.$description: Navy tint for a subtle wash on an ivory page.

200.$description: Secondary text on a navy surface — 11.06:1 against navy-900, 9.56:1 against navy-800.

300.$description: Muted text on a navy surface — 7.57:1 against navy-900, 6.55:1 against navy-800.

400.$description: Form-control outline on a navy surface — 4.50:1 against navy-900, 3.89:1 against navy-800. Both clear the 3:1 non-text minimum.

600.$description: Strong border and disabled text on a navy surface — 1.84:1. Decorative only.

700.$description: Default border and chart gridline on navy — 1.43:1. Also secondary text on ivory at 10.78:1.

800.$description: Raised surface on the dark theme — 1.16:1 against navy-900, which is the whole of the elevation signal available at this depth.

900.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — navy. Primary text on light surfaces at 15.37:1 against ivory-100 and 16.90:1 against white. Default dark-theme page surface.

950.$description: Sunken surface on the dark theme; deepest available navy. Ivory text on it reaches 17.04:1.

gold.$description: Brand gold. Anchor #C9A227 at step 500. Gold is a liturgical and honorific colour: it marks, it does not narrate. At step 500 it fails every WCAG text threshold on a light surface — 2.20:1 against ivory-100, 2.42:1 against white — so step 500 is restricted to decoration, iconography, rules and text on navy. Any gold that carries meaning as text on a light surface must use step 700 or darker.

100.$description: Gold wash for a highlighted card on an ivory page.

400.$description: Decorative gold on navy — 11.19:1 against navy-900, 9.67:1 against navy-800. Navy text on it reaches 11.19:1.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — gold. 6.98:1 against navy-900, so it IS text-safe on the dark theme. 2.20:1 against ivory-100 and 2.42:1 against white, so it is never text on a light surface.

600.$description: 2.99:1 against ivory-100: passes the 3:1 non-text threshold for icons, rules and borders at the boundary, still fails for text of any size. 5.14:1 against navy-900.

700.$description: Gold for TEXT on a light surface — 4.93:1 against ivory-100, 5.42:1 against white. Both pass AA at every size.

800.$description: 7.44:1 against ivory-100 — passes AAA for body text.

ivory.$description: Brand ivory. Anchor #F7F4EC at step 100. Ivory is the default page surface, not white: white cards sit on it, which gives a raised surface without a shadow. Warm enough to read as paper and stone, cool enough to keep navy text crisp.

50.$description: Near-white; the brightest permitted light surface.

100.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — ivory. Default light-theme page surface. Navy text on it is 15.37:1.

200.$description: Sunken surface, table banding, inset well. Navy text on it is 14.22:1.

300.$description: Default border and chart gridline on the light theme — 1.21:1 against ivory-100. Deliberate: a border is a hint, not an edge, and must not compete with content.

400.$description: Strong border on the light theme; hairline on a white card.

500.$description: Deepest ivory step. 8.46:1 against navy-900, so it is usable as text on a dark surface.

accent.$description: Interactive blue. Anchor #2E6BFF at step 500. Deliberately outside the navy and gold family: an accent that lives in the brand hue cannot be distinguished from a brand surface, and links would disappear into headers and footers. Reserved for interactive affordance and never used as decoration, because a colour reserved for interaction is the only way a user learns to trust it.

300.$description: Link colour on a raised dark surface — 5.70:1 against navy-800, where accent-400 falls to 4.14:1 and fails.

400.$description: Link and focus colour on the dark page surface — 4.80:1 against navy-900. Lifted above the computed ramp value so it clears AA with margin instead of sitting on the threshold. Valid on navy-900 only; see step 300 for navy-800.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — accent. 4.10:1 against ivory-100, 4.50:1 against white, 3.75:1 against navy-900. Passes the 3:1 non-text threshold for a focus ring, an icon or a border everywhere; is at the AA boundary for body text on white only. Body-size link text on a light surface uses step 600.

600.$description: Link text on the light theme — 6.10:1 against ivory-100, 6.70:1 against white.

700.$description: Hover for a link, pressed for a secondary button — 8.08:1 against ivory-100.

neutral.$description: Warm neutral. Anchor #8A8578 at step 500. Hue-matched to ivory rather than to navy, so greys do not read as dirty against a warm page. Carries all UI chrome that is not brand: dividers, placeholder text, disabled states, secondary iconography, chart axes.

400.$description: Disabled and placeholder text — 1.86:1 against ivory-100. Exempt from contrast minimums under WCAG 1.4.3 as an inactive component, and must never be used for content a user has to read.

500.$description: BRAND ANCHOR — neutral. 3.35:1 against ivory-100 and 3.68:1 against white, so it is the light-theme form-control outline. 4.59:1 against navy-900, so it doubles as a muted label on a dark surface.

600.$description: Chart axis on the light theme — 4.11:1 against ivory-100.

700.$description: Muted body text on the light theme — 5.97:1 against ivory-100, 6.56:1 against white. Passes AA at every size.

semantic.$description: Theme-aware roles. A component consumes these and nothing else. Every token name exists in both themes with the same meaning, so switching theme swaps values without touching markup.

light.$description: Default theme. Page surface is ivory-100; cards are white so they read as raised from a value step alone, without a shadow.

raised.$description: Card, popover, dialog, table header. 1.10:1 against page, so separation comes from the value step plus elevation.01 rather than from a border.

sunken.$description: Inset well, table banding, code block background.

overlay.$description: Modal scrim: 80% navy-900. Keeps the page legible behind a dialog while dropping it out of focus.

inverse.$description: A dark band inside a light page: hero, footer, pull quote.

primary.$description: Body copy and headings — 15.37:1 against surface.page, 16.90:1 against surface.raised.

secondary.$description: Supporting copy, table cells, metadata — 10.78:1 against surface.page, 11.85:1 against surface.raised.

muted.$description: Captions, helper text, timestamps — 5.97:1 against surface.page, 6.56:1 against surface.raised.

disabled.$description: Inactive controls only — 1.86:1 against surface.page. Not permitted for content a user must read.

link.$description: Inline link, resting — 6.10:1 against surface.page, 6.70:1 against surface.raised. Links are additionally underlined: colour is never the only signal, per WCAG 1.4.1.

link-raised.$description: Link inside a white card. Identical to text.link, because ivory-100 and white are only 1.10:1 apart so no step is needed — accent-600 measures 6.70:1 against white. The token exists anyway so that both themes expose the same shape: a component can always use link-raised inside a card without a theme check, which matters because the dark theme genuinely does need a different value there.

link-visited.$description: 8.33:1 against surface.page, 9.16:1 against surface.raised. Distinct from link in both hue and lightness so the distinction survives deuteranopia.

brand.$description: Gold used AS TEXT on a light surface — 4.93:1 against surface.page, 5.42:1 against surface.raised. Never substitute gold-500 here.

on-gold.$description: Text on a gold-500 fill — 6.98:1. Navy on gold is the only approved combination; white on gold is 2.42:1 and fails.

default.$description: Hairline between same-level surfaces — 1.21:1 against surface.page.

strong.$description: Emphasis hairline — 1.43:1 against surface.page. Not sufficient for a form control, which needs 3:1; inputs use border.input.

input.$description: Text-input and select outline — 3.35:1 against surface.page, 3.68:1 against surface.raised. Clears the 3:1 non-text requirement in WCAG 1.4.11 on both.

focus.$description: Focus ring — 4.10:1 against surface.page, 4.50:1 against surface.raised. Both above the 3:1 minimum for focus appearance in WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11.

divider.$description: Table row rule and section separator — 1.08:1 against surface.page.

state.$description: Status colours. Each state ships a foreground verified at 4.5:1 or better against the light page surface, and a tint for the fill behind a banner against which navy text is verified. Meaning is never carried by colour alone: every state pairs with an icon and a text label, per WCAG 1.4.1.

success-tint.$description: Banner fill. Navy-900 text on it is 14.43:1.

warning.$description: 4.92:1 against surface.page, 5.40:1 against surface.raised. Darkened from the obvious amber, which sits near 3.8:1 and fails body text.

warning-tint.$description: Banner fill. Navy-900 text on it is 14.76:1.

danger-tint.$description: Banner fill. Navy-900 text on it is 13.82:1.

info-tint.$description: Banner fill. Navy-900 text on it is 14.23:1.

dark.$description: Navy theme for heroes, dashboards, night-time kiosk use and prefers-color-scheme: dark. Not a mirror image of the light theme: a drop shadow is near-invisible on navy, so elevation is carried by a lighter surface value and a hairline top edge instead. See elevation.json. A second divergence is link colour, which steps up one ramp position on a raised surface because navy-800 lifts the background luminance enough to drop accent-400 below 4.5:1.

overlay.$description: Modal scrim on navy — deeper than navy-950 so a dialog separates from a dark page.

inverse.$description: A light band inside a dark page.

muted.$description: 7.57:1 against surface.page, 6.55:1 against surface.raised — passes AAA on both.

link.$description: 4.80:1 against surface.page. On surface.raised it drops to 4.14:1 and fails — use text.link-raised there.

link-raised.$description: Link inside a dark card, popover or dialog — 5.70:1 against surface.raised.

brand.$description: On navy, brand gold IS text-safe — 6.98:1 against surface.page, 6.04:1 against surface.raised. The light theme must use gold-700 instead, which is why this token exists rather than a shared value.

input.$description: Form-control outline — 4.50:1 against surface.page, 3.89:1 against surface.raised. Clears 3:1 on both.

focus.$description: Focus ring — 4.80:1 against surface.page, 4.14:1 against surface.raised. A focus indicator needs 3:1, so both pass.

success-tint.$description: Banner fill — 1.26:1 against surface.page. Its own foreground is 7.22:1 and ivory text on it is 12.24:1.

warning-tint.$description: Banner fill — 1.25:1 against surface.page, 7.18:1 against state.warning.

danger-tint.$description: Banner fill — 1.06:1 against surface.page, 6.28:1 against state.danger.

info-tint.$description: Banner fill — 1.13:1 against surface.page, 7.80:1 against state.info.

church.$description: Church-context pairs: the colour roles a funeral, cemetery, parish or basilica surface needs, expressed as foreground/background couples rather than single values. Each pair is verified by tools/contrast_check.py against the minimum declared for it in $extensions. These are UI roles for a page ABOUT a context — not the liturgical season palette, which lives in colors.church.json.

funeral.$description: Funeral and bereavement. Restrained to the point of austerity: no gold, no saturated accent, no celebratory green. A family reading this page at the worst moment of their life should not be asked to process a colour that means anything. Ivory on near-black navy, the highest text contrast in the system, no decoration.

text.$description: 17.04:1 against surface. Deliberately AAA and then some: this audience is often elderly, often distressed, and often reading on a phone in a bright church porch.

accent.$description: Links stay inside the navy family rather than switching to blue: a bright interactive colour on a funeral page reads as commerce.

cemetery.$description: Cemetery and memorial garden. Stone and weathered bronze: warm neutral surfaces with a muted gold that reads as an inscription rather than as a highlight. Legibility in direct daylight is the governing constraint, which is why the surface is pale and the text near-black.

text.$description: 14.22:1 against surface — high contrast survives glare on a graveside phone.

parish.$description: Parish life: rotas, newsletters, notices, giving. The warmest and most ordinary of the contexts — ivory surfaces, navy text, inscription gold for emphasis, accent blue for the interactive layer. This is the default look of a ViaVitae parish page and the starting point for any new one.

basilica.$description: Basilica, cathedral and heritage: the ceremonial register. Navy surface with gold and ivory — the inverse of the parish context. Reserved for heritage content, building history, visiting information, and anything where the architecture rather than the congregation is the subject.

accent.$description: 6.98:1 against surface. Gold is text-safe on navy, which is precisely why the ceremonial register is dark.

chart.$description: Categorical data-visualisation series, ordered. Two properties hold by construction and are re-verified by tools/contrast_check.py: every series clears 3:1 against its chart surface (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, non-text contrast), and consecutive series are separated by at least 2.28:1 in relative luminance so a stacked bar or an adjacent legend entry stays legible in greyscale and under colour-vision deficiency. Hue alone never carries meaning: a chart must label its series directly or ship a monochrome alternative, per WCAG 1.4.1. Eight series maximum; beyond eight the ramp restarts and the chart is wrong.

light.$description: Series for a chart drawn on color.semantic.light.surface.page (#F7F4EC). Luminance staircase alternating dark, light, dark, light. Worst on-surface contrast 3.06:1; worst consecutive separation 2.28:1.

2.$description: Gold series — 3.81:1. Separated from series 1 by 2.97:1.

3.$description: Teal series — 9.57:1. Separated from series 2 by 2.51:1.

4.$description: Crimson series — 3.47:1. Separated from series 3 by 2.76:1.

5.$description: Plum series — 8.33:1. Separated from series 4 by 2.40:1.

6.$description: Olive series — 3.21:1. Separated from series 5 by 2.60:1.

7.$description: Sienna series — 7.31:1. Separated from series 6 by 2.28:1, the tightest pair in the ramp.

8.$description: Slate series — 3.06:1. Separated from series 7 by 2.39:1.

dark.$description: Series for a chart drawn on color.semantic.dark.surface.page (#0E1B3D). Inverted staircase alternating light, dark, light, dark. Worst on-surface contrast 3.59:1; worst consecutive separation 2.47:1.

2.$description: Gold series — 3.59:1. Separated from series 1 by 2.54:1.

3.$description: Teal series — 10.08:1. Separated from series 2 by 2.81:1.

4.$description: Crimson series — 4.03:1. Separated from series 3 by 2.50:1.

5.$description: Plum series — 11.16:1. Separated from series 4 by 2.77:1.

6.$description: Olive series — 4.44:1. Separated from series 5 by 2.51:1.

7.$description: Sienna series — 12.08:1. Separated from series 6 by 2.72:1.

8.$description: Slate series — 4.90:1. Separated from series 7 by 2.47:1.

grid.$description: Chart gridline on a light surface — 1.21:1. Deliberately below the 3:1 threshold: a gridline is scaffolding and must not compete with the data.

grid-dark.$description: Chart gridline on a dark surface — 1.43:1.

axis.$description: Axis line and tick, light theme — 4.11:1 against surface.page.

axis-dark.$description: Axis line and tick, dark theme — 7.57:1 against surface.page.

label.$description: Axis label and data label, light theme — 5.97:1 against surface.page.

label-dark.$description: Axis label and data label, dark theme — 11.06:1 against surface.page.

com.viavitae.contrast-pairs.$description: The contrast contract. tools/contrast_check.py reads this list, resolves every alias to a literal hex value, computes the WCAG 2.x contrast ratio and fails the build when a pair falls below its declared minimum. Adding a semantic text or foreground token without adding its pair here is a review blocker — the tool cannot verify what is not declared. Minimums: 4.5 body text (WCAG 1.4.3), 3.0 large text at 24px or 18.66px bold (1.4.3), 7.0 AAA body text (1.4.6), 3.0 non-text UI components and graphical objects (1.4.11), 3.0 focus appearance (2.4.11), 1.3 minimum separation between adjacent chart series.

text-on-surface.note: MEASURED AND EXEMPT, not unmeasured. 1.86:1. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive user-interface components, and a disabled control is inactive by definition. The exemption does not extend to placeholder text on a required field, which is content the user must read and must use text.muted instead. Declared with a minimum of 1.0 so the exemption is a recorded decision with a number attached rather than an absence that a reviewer has to notice.
MEASURED AND EXEMPT. 1.84:1. Inactive components only, on the same terms as the light theme.
AAA by policy: bereavement content is frequently read by distressed and elderly users, often on a small screen in poor light.

chart-series-separation.$description: Adjacent series must stay distinguishable when a chart is printed in greyscale or viewed under a colour-vision deficiency. Measured as a WCAG contrast ratio between the two series colours. 1.3:1 is the floor; both ramps ship at 2.28:1 or better because hue alone is not a reliable channel.

prohibited.$description: Combinations that look right and fail. Listed explicitly so a tool and a reviewer can reject them by name instead of relying on someone remembering the arithmetic. tools/contrast_check.py asserts each of these is still below its threshold: if a palette change makes one of them pass, the entry is stale and must be removed or the guidance rewritten.

entries.reason: Brand gold at step 500 fails AA, AA-large and the 3:1 non-text threshold on ivory. This is the single most likely contrast regression in the system, because gold is the colour a designer reaches for first.
As above on a white card.
White text on a gold fill fails. A gold button carries navy-900 text, per text.on-gold.
Accent 500 sits at 4.10:1 on ivory. Permitted for a focus ring, an icon or a 24px display heading; body-size link text must use accent 600.
Accent 400 drops to 4.14:1 inside a dark card. Use text.link-raised there; this is why that token exists.
Navy on navy. Elevation on a dark surface is carried by the surface step and a hairline top edge, never by a change in text colour.
Disabled grey on ivory at 1.86:1. Exempt under WCAG 1.4.3 as an inactive component — the exemption does not extend to placeholder text for a required field.
